scope: Selected books, films and television works with a documented connection to a real system in the 143-row historical catalog. This is an evidence index, not a census or popularity ranking of science fiction.

works.title: Mission of Gravity
works.creator: Hal Clement
works.note: Mesklin is a fictional world conceived around 61 Cygni; a historical putative companion informed the premise, not a confirmed planet. The book edition followed 1953 serialization.
works.source: Lunar and Planetary Institute, Comparative Climatology III (2018)

works.title: Barbarella
works.creator: Roger Vadim
works.note: NASA identifies Tau Ceti as a setting of the 1968 film. The film's imagined setting is not an astronomical observation.
works.source: NASA Science, The Science Behind Project Hail Mary

works.title: Star Trek / Vulcan
works.creator: Star Trek franchise
works.note: The 1991 date marks Gene Roddenberry's published identification of 40 Eridani A as Vulcan's host, not the television franchise's 1966 debut. Vulcan remains fictional.
works.source: StarTrek.com, Vulcan-like Planet Found... for Real

works.title: Star Trek: The Next Generation / Wolf 359
works.creator: Star Trek franchise
works.note: The Borg battle in The Best of Both Worlds is placed at the real Wolf 359 star; the battle is fictional.
works.source: StarTrek.com, White Dwarfs, Red Dwarfs, and Blue Giants, Oh My!

works.title: Rocheworld
works.creator: Robert L. Forward
works.note: The publisher describes a voyage to a fictional double planet circling Barnard's Star. Year denotes the expanded Rocheworld edition.

works.title: Babylon 5
works.creator: J. Michael Straczynski
works.note: NASA/JPL identifies Epsilon Eridani as the location of the fictional Babylon 5 station. Year denotes the series premiere.
works.source: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Double the Rubble (2008)

works.title: Screamers
works.creator: Christian Duguay
works.note: The film distributor's synopsis names the fictional Sirius 6B mining planet. It is not the catalog's stellar component Sirius B or a known planet.

works.title: Avatar
works.creator: James Cameron
works.note: The franchise's official Pandorapedia places fictional Pandora in the real Alpha Centauri system. The moon and Polyphemus are fictional.

works.title: Proxima
works.creator: Stephen Baxter
works.note: The novel places settlers on fictional Proxima IV around the real Proxima Centauri.

works.title: Aurora
works.creator: Kim Stanley Robinson
works.note: The ship's destination is the Tau Ceti system; Aurora is a fictional moon in the novel.

works.title: Trident's Forge
works.creator: Patrick S. Tomlinson
works.note: The publisher places the fictional colony Tau Ceti G and its first-contact story in the real Tau Ceti system.
works.source: Penguin Random House / Angry Robot, publisher catalogue

works.title: Project Hail Mary
works.creator: Andy Weir
works.note: Tau Ceti is the mission destination; fictional Erid is associated with 40 Eridani A. These are two links from one book.
works.source: NASA Science, book/film explainer; Penguin Random House author interview

works.title: Braking Day
works.creator: Adam Oyebanji
works.note: The publisher describes three generation ships approaching a fictional planet orbiting the real Tau Ceti star. Year marks the first ebook edition.

works.title: The Scourge Between Stars
works.creator: Ness Brown
works.note: The publisher's synopsis names a failed colony on fictional Proxima b; this is a literary premise, not a claim about the actual planet.

works.title: Project Hail Mary (film)
works.creator: Phil Lord & Christopher Miller
works.note: NASA discusses the 2026 film adaptation and its use of Tau Ceti and 40 Eridani A. It is counted separately from the 2021 novel, but shares the same fictional premise.
works.source: NASA Science, The Science Behind Project Hail Mary
